paragraphs: Knowledge graphs organize information as entities connected by relations. Reasoning systems often need separate models for different graphs, making knowledge difficult to transfer between settings. KG-ICL addresses this fragmentation by using an example supplied in context to help a shared model understand the relation involved in a query.

The method constructs a prompt graph around an example fact related to the query. A unified tokenizer maps the entities and relations in that graph to predefined tokens, supporting queries involving previously unseen entities and relations. Two message-passing neural networks then divide the work: one encodes the prompt, and the other performs reasoning over the knowledge graph.

Evaluation covers 43 knowledge graphs in both transductive and inductive settings. KG-ICL outperforms the comparison methods on most datasets, supporting its ability to transfer across varied graphs and reasoning conditions. The central contribution is a way to make contextual examples useful for graph reasoning, with shared representations that reduce dependence on the identities present in a particular graph.
neurips-2024-a-prompt-based-knowledge-gr.tldr: KG-ICL uses example-centered graph prompts to transfer reasoning across knowledge graphs, outperforming baselines on most of 43 evaluated graphs.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can create convincing images while omitting requested objects or failing to satisfy layout constraints. Fine editing also commonly requires detailed maps that are laborious to prepare. This paper introduces Factor Graph Diffusion Models, which jointly model images and conditioning information such as semantic labels, sketches, depth, and surface normals.

A factor graph decomposes that joint distribution into connected components. This structure supports sampling procedures that improve prompt compliance and allows images and their conditions to be generated together. The authors also introduce attention distillation, encouraging the components' attention maps to agree so that the generated image and conditioning information remain consistent.

An implementation adapts pretrained Stable Diffusion using COCO and reports 15% higher object recall while retaining generalization ability. Models trained from scratch on four datasets also produce high image quality and diversity. Beyond these results, the framework supports partially automated editing, labeled-data generation, training with missing data, and adding conditioning variables with little or no change to the existing structure.
neurips-2024-adapting-diffusion-models-f.tldr: Factor Graph Diffusion Models jointly generate images and conditioning maps to improve prompt compliance and enable more flexible image control.

paragraphs: Long-tailed learning deals with datasets in which some classes have many examples and others have few. A model trained on one balance of common and rare classes can struggle when that balance changes at test time. Users may also prefer different compromises between performance on frequent head classes and scarce tail classes.

The proposed approach uses hypernetworks to generate a collection of diverse expert models. These experts are intended to span possible distribution scenarios, and their ensemble is optimized to adapt to the test distribution. The system also produces a dedicated model solution that reflects a user's preferred balance between head and tail performance.

The experiments report higher achievable performance, effective handling of distribution shift, and controllable adjustments to user preferences. These findings support treating adaptation and user control as connected parts of long-tailed learning. The practical contribution is a framework in which the chosen solution can vary with both the data distribution and the desired class trade-off, rather than committing to a single compromise during training.
neurips-2024-breaking-long-tailed-learni.tldr: Hypernetwork-generated experts let long-tailed classifiers adapt to changing class distributions and user preferences about common versus rare classes.

paragraphs: Blind image deblurring must recover a sharp image while also estimating the blur that produced the observation. Many deep learning approaches rely on known sharp images during training. This paper develops a self-supervised alternative, where the main challenge is preventing the model from overfitting without that direct reference.

The training signal comes from an exact relationship connecting the blurred image, the unknown sharp image, and the blur kernel across consecutive scales. A cross-scale consistency loss encourages these quantities to agree across resolutions. Both the image and kernel are represented with implicit neural representations, whose resolution-independent form makes the multiscale computation consistent and efficient.

Training proceeds progressively from coarse scales to fine ones, combining that schedule with the consistency constraint. Extensive experiments show significant improvements over existing self-supervised deblurring methods. The result demonstrates the value of using relationships within the image formation problem itself as supervision: agreement across scales helps constrain recovery even when ground-truth sharp images are unavailable.
neurips-2024-cross-scale-self-supervised.tldr: Cross-scale consistency and implicit neural representations enable blind image deblurring without ground-truth sharp images.

paragraphs: Animals can respond to changing situations by selecting previously learned task knowledge. This paper studies how comparable flexibility might emerge in a neural network without separately specifying its task modules. The authors analyze a linear network whose weights and gates learn together through gradient descent, with gates constrained to be nonnegative, bounded, and faster adapting than the weights.

Under these conditions, weights organize into modules specializing in encountered tasks or subtasks. The gates develop representations that select the appropriate modules. An analytical reduction reveals a reinforcing interaction: fast gates protect earlier knowledge and encourage specialization, while specialized weights make the gates update faster.

Task switching becomes faster with training and changes with curriculum block size, echoing findings from cognitive neuroscience. The resulting abstractions also support generalization by composing tasks and subtasks. The authors extend their findings to a nonlinear network switching between two tasks. Together, these results offer a theory of how joint learning at different timescales can produce flexible task selection under the studied architectural constraints.
neurips-2024-flexible-task-abstractions-.tldr: Fast, bounded gates and jointly learned weights can self-organize into reusable task modules that support flexible switching and composition.

paragraphs: A useful language model needs to provide helpful responses while maintaining honesty. This paper addresses both goals through evaluation and methods for changing model behavior. The authors first establish principles for honest responses and introduce HoneSet, an evaluation collection containing 930 queries across six categories.

Their training-free method, Curiosity-Driven Prompting, asks a model to express confusion and uncertainty about a query before improving its response. This gives uncertainty an explicit role in producing the answer. A separate fine-tuning method uses two stages inspired by curriculum learning: first teaching the distinction between honest and dishonest behavior, then teaching more helpful responding.

Experiments show that both approaches improve helpfulness while maintaining honesty. The contribution is therefore twofold: a structured way to assess honesty and two routes for improving the balance between honest and useful answers. One route operates through prompting, while the other changes the model through staged training, giving the study relevance to both training-free and fine-tuning settings.
neurips-2024-honestllm-toward-an-honest-.tldr: HonestLLM introduces an honesty benchmark and two methods that improve helpfulness while maintaining honesty in experiments.

paragraphs: Generating images with readable text requires more than producing realistic visual content. Many systems guide diffusion models using images of text rendered in standard fonts. This paper investigates how that guidance behaves, examining its input encoding, its changing role during denoising, and the features it produces.

The authors find that text guidance has properties distinct from familiar controls such as edges and depth. They also find that its role changes across denoising stages and that its output features differ in frequency content from the U-Net decoder's base and skip features. These observations motivate TextGen, which uses Fourier analysis to emphasize relevant information and suppress noise in the control features.

TextGen also separates generation into two stages to accommodate the different roles of guidance over time. The authors introduce a lightweight training dataset alongside the framework. Their method achieves state-of-the-art Chinese and English text-generation performance, supporting the idea that improving how control information is represented and scheduled can improve the resulting text images.
neurips-2024-how-control-information-inf.tldr: TextGen improves Chinese and English text-image generation by refining control features and matching guidance to different denoising stages.

paragraphs: State estimation in vision and robotics may need to keep several plausible explanations of an observation alive at once. Particle methods represent those alternatives explicitly. A particle smoother can use information from both earlier and later observations, making it attractive for offline analysis, but traditional smoothers have depended on manually engineered dynamics and observation models.

This paper makes particle smoothing trainable from end to end. Its two-filter design combines particle streams moving forward and backward through time. During resampling, it uses stratification and importance weights to obtain low-variance gradient estimates for neural dynamics and observation models, helping learning signals propagate across long sequences.

The resulting mixture density particle smoother is evaluated on city-scale global vehicle localization using real videos and maps. It is substantially more accurate than state-of-the-art particle filters and search-based comparison methods. The findings show how learned smoothing can combine multiple hypotheses with evidence from both temporal directions, improving localization in the studied offline setting.
neurips-2024-learning-to-be-smooth-an-en.tldr: A differentiable particle smoother learns to combine past and future evidence, improving city-scale vehicle localization from videos and maps.

paragraphs: Learning several component procedures does not automatically mean a model can efficiently learn to combine them. This paper examines that distinction using four discrete tasks, each requiring a composition of smaller subtasks. The study trains LLaMA models and prompts GPT-4 and Gemini to measure how effectively they reuse primitives available in the component tasks.

The results reveal substantial sample inefficiency in the evaluated settings. LLaMA needs more examples to learn the composed task than would be required to relearn all its subtasks from scratch. Few-example prompting is also unreliable, with failures in executing subtasks and in correcting errors during multiple rounds of code generation.

A complexity-theoretic analysis supports these observations by studying the sample inefficiency of gradient descent in memorizing feedforward models. The combined evidence highlights a gap between exposure to reusable primitives and efficient composition. Its scope is the studied tasks, models, and theoretical setting; the contribution is an empirical and analytical account of that gap, rather than a claim that Transformers cannot compose algorithms.
neurips-2024-limits-of-transformer-langu.tldr: Across four discrete tasks, tested Transformer language models struggle to efficiently reuse component procedures when learning their composition.

paragraphs: Multi-armed bandit methods learn which actions yield better rewards, but their observations may require privacy protection and may also be corrupted. This paper studies those problems together, allowing rewards to be heavy-tailed. It distinguishes corruption after a locally private response is produced from corruption of raw data before privacy protection is applied.

The authors first establish tight high-probability bounds for estimating a mean in both settings. They then derive nearly tight bounds, up to logarithmic factors, for online regret and offline decision suboptimality. These characterize worst-case achievable performance, and systematic simulations corroborate the theoretical results.

A central finding is that corruption after privacy protection is harder in the minimax sense than corruption beforehand. The analysis also yields tight bounds when corruption can occur on both sides of the privacy mechanism. As a further result, the paper identifies a flaw in earlier work and supplies a correct tight regret bound for locally private online bandits with heavy-tailed rewards and no Huber corruption.
neurips-2024-locally-private-and-robust-.tldr: Tight performance bounds show that bandit learning is harder when data corruption follows local privacy protection than when it precedes it.

paragraphs: Continual learning requires a model to absorb new tasks while preserving earlier knowledge. This creates tension between responsiveness to new information and stability of what has already been learned. The paper approaches that tension through the geometry of the training loss, seeking solutions that remain stable under changes to model parameters.

Existing sharpness-aware training can improve generalization, but the authors point out that zeroth-order sharpness alone can favor sharper solutions over flatter ones in some situations. They introduce Continual Flatness, or C-Flat, to encourage a flatter loss landscape tailored to continual learning. The method is designed as a plug-in that can be invoked with one line of code.

The study presents a framework spanning continual-learning categories and compares C-Flat with loss-minimum optimizers and other approaches based on flat minima. It improves continual-learning performance in almost all reported cases. These findings support using a more suitable flatness objective to strengthen existing methods, while preserving the distinction between broad experimental success and improvement in every possible case.
neurips-2024-make-continual-learning-str.tldr: C-Flat encourages a loss landscape suited to continual learning and improves existing methods in almost all reported comparisons.

paragraphs: Models that handle images and text face safety challenges that may be missed by narrowly focused tests. MLLMGuard provides a broader evaluation suite covering English and Chinese across privacy, bias, toxicity, truthfulness, and legality. It combines an image-text dataset, tools for running inference, and an automated evaluator.

The dataset draws primarily from sources such as social media and incorporates adversarial testing through both text and images. Human experts carefully annotate the examples. This construction aims to produce challenging, high-quality tests and reduce inaccurate evaluation associated with leakage from existing open datasets. The paper also questions evaluating a model with itself, citing GPT-4V's preference for its own responses.

The authors introduce GuardRank as a lightweight alternative evaluator and report significantly higher evaluation accuracy than GPT-4. Tests across 13 advanced models reveal substantial remaining safety shortcomings. The suite's contribution is to make several distinct safety dimensions assessable within one bilingual framework, while treating evaluator quality as part of the measurement problem.
neurips-2024-mllmguard-a-multi-dimension.tldr: MLLMGuard evaluates image-text models across five safety dimensions in English and Chinese, revealing substantial shortcomings in 13 tested models.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a 3D object from multiple views requires information to remain consistent across those views. The authors observe that existing Gaussian reconstruction models can produce inconsistent views and blurred textures. They attribute this partly to architectures that sacrifice information propagation across views to accommodate computationally expensive components.

MVGamba uses a lightweight state-space model with recurrent-style processing to reconstruct a sequence of 3D Gaussians. As it generates that sequence, it propagates context containing information from multiple views, allowing cross-view refinement. Linear complexity supports long Gaussian sequences for representing fine detail. Combined with existing multi-view diffusion models, the same reconstruction framework supports generation from one image, several sparse images, or text.

Across the evaluated 3D generation scenarios, MVGamba outperforms state-of-the-art comparison methods with approximately one-tenth of the model size. The findings support sequence modeling as an effective way to combine detailed Gaussian representations with efficient information sharing across views. The reported advantage connects reconstruction quality and model compactness within a single design.
neurips-2024-mvgamba-unify-3d-content-ge.tldr: MVGamba uses state-space sequence modeling for multi-view Gaussian reconstruction, outperforming tested baselines with roughly one-tenth of their model size.

paragraphs: Geometric transformations in real-world vision can be difficult to describe with manageable equations. Neural Isometries addresses this by learning a representation in which geometrically related observations are connected by simpler, structure-preserving transformations. An autoencoder maps observations into this latent space, moving part of the difficulty into representation learning.

The training constraints make transformations between encodings preserve a learned inner product and commute with a learned functional operator. In plain terms, the transformations must respect both a learned notion of geometry and an additional operation on the representation. The construction parallels the relationship between rigid transformations and the Laplacian.

The learned space supports self-supervised representation learning. A standard equivariant network operating within it achieves results comparable to carefully handcrafted networks for complex nonlinear symmetries. The transformations between encodings also retain information about motion in the world: the authors use their coefficients to predict camera poses between adjacent scene views. This shows that the representation can support both downstream processing and direct estimation of geometric relationships.
neurips-2024-neural-isometries-taming-tr.tldr: Neural Isometries learns a latent space where complex geometric transformations become structured maps usable for equivariant learning and camera-pose estimation.

paragraphs: A regression method can stop benefiting from additional smoothness in the function it is trying to learn. This saturation effect means its error no longer reaches the best theoretically achievable rate for sufficiently smooth targets. The paper studies this behavior for spectral algorithms when sample size n scales like dimension d raised to a power gamma.

The authors establish an improved minimax lower bound for kernel regression in this regime. They show that gradient flow with early stopping reaches that bound up to a logarithmic factor. They also derive matching upper and lower convergence rates for a broad class of optimally tuned spectral algorithms with different qualification parameters tau.

As gamma varies, the exact rates exhibit recurring plateaus and a polynomial approximation barrier. The analysis identifies saturation in the large-dimensional setting when the source-condition parameter s exceeds tau, compared with the stated fixed-dimensional condition s greater than twice tau. This makes precise how growing dimension changes the smoothness conditions under which an algorithm's statistical performance saturates.
neurips-2024-on-the-saturation-effects-o.tldr: Exact error rates reveal how growing dimension changes saturation in spectral regression, while early-stopped gradient flow nearly attains the minimax bound.

paragraphs: An online forecaster repeatedly predicts probabilities over K possible classes. U-calibration asks whether those predictions have low regret across all bounded proper losses simultaneously, rather than under just one scoring rule. This paper determines the optimal growth rate of that error over T prediction rounds.

Earlier work provided a bound of order K times the square root of T. The authors show that Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader achieves the smaller order square root of KT. A matching lower bound, built using a particular proper loss, establishes that this dependence is optimal. The lower-bound construction also proves optimality of the algorithm in a related online-learning setting with an adversary having finitely many choices.

Additional assumptions on the loss functions allow stronger guarantees. For Lipschitz proper losses, the paper establishes an optimal logarithmic dependence on T; it also gives a logarithmic upper bound for a specified class of decomposable proper losses. Further bounds use low covering numbers. These results distinguish the general worst-case rate from improvements available when the loss family has additional structure.
neurips-2024-optimal-multiclass-u-calibr.tldr: The paper proves the optimal multiclass U-calibration rate is proportional to √(KT), with stronger bounds for structured loss families.

paragraphs: Generating a graph raises an ordering problem: changing node labels should not change the graph being modeled. Autoregressive methods are effective but often sensitive to ordering, while existing diffusion methods can require many denoising steps and additional features. PARD combines autoregressive generation with diffusion while preserving permutation invariance.

The method uses a unique partial order over nodes and edges identified from graph structure. It generates the graph block by block, with a shared diffusion model determining each block's distribution conditional on earlier blocks. An equivariant network maintains the required behavior under relabeling. A higher-order graph transformer combines transformer processing with PPGN and supports parallel training across blocks.

Without extra features, PARD achieves state-of-the-art results on both molecular and non-molecular datasets. It also scales to MOSES, which contains 1.9 million molecules. The contribution is a way to exploit structural ordering without becoming dependent on arbitrary node numbering, combining sequential graph construction with diffusion-based modeling inside each block.
neurips-2024-pard-permutation-invariant-.tldr: PARD generates graphs block by block with shared diffusion, combining autoregressive modeling with invariance to arbitrary node relabeling.

paragraphs: Image restoration benefits from contextual information, but attention can spend computation on regions unrelated to the damaged content being reconstructed. This becomes particularly costly at high resolution. SemanIR focuses attention on semantically related image patches and reuses those relationships across multiple transformer blocks.

At the beginning of each transformer stage, the model builds a sparse dictionary recording important semantic connections for every degraded patch. Subsequent blocks in that stage share the dictionary, so their attention calculations consider only the related components it contains. The strategy combines selective attention with reuse of the selected connections, achieving linear attention complexity within each window.

Experiments across six image-restoration tasks report state-of-the-art performance, supported by both numerical comparisons and visual results. These findings suggest that selecting relevant context can improve restoration while making attention more efficient. The computational claim applies specifically to attention within windows, and the shared dictionary operates within a stage, making the scope of the efficiency mechanism concrete.
neurips-2024-sharing-key-semantics-in-tr.tldr: SemanIR shares sparse semantic connections across transformer blocks to improve image restoration with linear attention complexity within each window.

paragraphs: Digitizing an object involves recovering its shape, materials, and surrounding illumination from photographs. These properties jointly determine appearance, so estimating them together is central to reproducing the object under different lighting. SplitNeRF addresses this task using images with known camera poses, captured under fixed lighting.

The method brings the split sum approximation from physically based image-based lighting into a Neural Radiance Field pipeline. A single scene-specific multilayer perceptron represents pre-integrated environmental lighting at arbitrary resolutions. A regularizer built around efficient Monte Carlo sampling helps it model that lighting accurately. A related sampling-based regularizer also supervises predictions of self-occlusion.

Experiments demonstrate effective and efficient recovery of geometry, material properties, and lighting. The method achieves state-of-the-art relighting quality after approximately one hour of training on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. This result links the proposed representation and regularization to the practical aim of changing an object's illumination after reconstruction, under the stated posed-image and fixed-lighting input conditions.
neurips-2024-splitnerf-split-sum-approxi.tldr: SplitNeRF jointly estimates shape, materials, and lighting from posed images, achieving state-of-the-art relighting after roughly one hour of training.

paragraphs: Understanding a table image involves locating the table, recovering its structure, and interpreting its contents. Separate task-specific systems can turn these closely connected activities into complicated workflows. TabPedia brings them together in a large vision-language model designed to handle both visual perception and reasoning about tables.

Its concept synergy mechanism treats the different tasks and visual embeddings from multiple sources as concepts within a shared framework. This allows table detection, structure recognition, querying, and question answering to draw on corresponding visual clues. The aim is to let perception and comprehension support each other through the information available in those embeddings.

The authors also introduce ComTQA, a table visual-question-answering benchmark containing approximately 9,000 question-answer pairs for evaluating more realistic scenarios. Quantitative and qualitative experiments across public benchmarks validate TabPedia on both perception and comprehension tasks. The findings support integrating these tasks through a language-model-based framework, with coordinated access to visual information playing a central role.
neurips-2024-tabpedia-towards-comprehens.tldr: TabPedia unifies table perception and comprehension through shared concepts and introduces a roughly 9,000-pair table question-answering benchmark.

paragraphs: A graph foundation model aims to use one backbone across different graphs and tasks. A major obstacle is that nodes from different domains can have very different features. Text-space approaches use natural language as a shared feature space, drawing inspiration from multimodal systems that align different kinds of information with language.

This paper focuses on the evidence needed to evaluate that strategy. Existing research lacks both a comprehensive benchmark with consistent problem settings and enough datasets to examine performance across diverse conditions. Without those shared resources, it is difficult to compare methods clearly or assess their practical value.

The authors contribute new text-space graph datasets and a broad evaluation under unified settings. Their empirical study produces insights intended to guide subsequent research. The contribution is primarily an evaluation foundation: a more consistent basis for studying how well text can unify graph features and support transfer across tasks and domains. It expands the resources available for comparison without claiming that one approach is universally best.
neurips-2024-text-space-graph-foundation.tldr: New datasets and unified evaluations provide a more comprehensive benchmark for graph foundation models that use text as a shared feature space.

paragraphs: Building a complex CAD model often requires time-consuming creation of simpler intermediate parts. Text2CAD seeks to make that process more accessible by generating parametric CAD designs from natural-language instructions. Its inputs range from broad descriptions suitable for beginners to detailed specifications that express a designer's intended construction.

The authors create a text-annotation pipeline for DeepCAD using Mistral and LLaVA-NeXT. The resulting dataset contains approximately 170,000 models and 660,000 text annotations. Descriptions span overall shapes through precise instructions involving coordinates, radii, and extrusion distances. This range connects the same design-generation problem to multiple levels of user expertise.

An end-to-end autoregressive transformer converts the input text into a sequential parametric CAD design. Evaluation considers visual quality, parameter precision, and geometric accuracy, reflecting that a useful design must be assessed beyond appearance alone. The reported findings indicate promise for AI-assisted design. The central contribution combines a broad instruction dataset with a model that generates the structured sequence defining a CAD object.
neurips-2024-text2cad-generating-sequent.tldr: Text2CAD generates sequential parametric CAD designs from instructions ranging from broad shape descriptions to detailed construction specifications.

paragraphs: Answering a factual question about an image can require satisfying several visual and textual conditions together. This paper uses that perspective to investigate where multimodal language models store relevant information and how image information reaches those locations. It extends causal information tracing to the multimodal setting and introduces VQA-Constraints, containing 9,700 annotated visual questions.

The authors study LLaVA and multimodal Phi-2. In these models, they find important information-storage roles for MLP and self-attention blocks in much earlier layers than the middle-layer MLPs emphasized in prior language-only studies. They also identify a consistent small subset of vision-encoder tokens responsible for transferring image information to those causal blocks.

To validate the discovered mechanisms, the paper introduces MultEdit, which targets the identified blocks to correct errors and add long-tailed information. This connects the tracing results to an intervention that changes model knowledge. The findings provide a focused account of information flow in the two studied models on factual visual question answering, alongside tools for examining that process.
neurips-2024-understanding-information-s.tldr: Causal tracing identifies early-layer information storage and a small set of image-transfer tokens in two multimodal models, enabling targeted knowledge edits.

paragraphs: Urban research uses many kinds of data to study problems such as air quality and built-up areas. Researchers often process those sources separately for each task. This fragmentation makes large benchmarks harder to construct and makes information from different modalities harder to combine, slowing the comparison and development of methods.

UrbanDataLayer provides standardized data structures and processing pipelines for city data. Its unified format gives researchers a common basis for preparing datasets and combining modalities. The approach targets the data-engineering work that sits between raw urban information and the models used to analyze it.

The authors demonstrate the data layer through four distinct urban tasks. These applications serve as evidence for the usefulness of a shared pipeline across different problems. The intended broader benefit is more efficient, standardized research, including easier construction of large-scale benchmarks and support for multimodal urban foundation models. The contribution is shared data infrastructure that makes those activities easier to pursue, rather than a separate predictive model for each urban task.
neurips-2024-urbandatalayer-a-unified-da.tldr: UrbanDataLayer standardizes city-data structures and pipelines to make multimodal integration and large-scale urban benchmarks easier to build.

paragraphs: Language models retain key-value information during generation so they can attend to previous context. YOCO redesigns how that information is produced and reused to reduce GPU memory requirements. Its decoder-decoder architecture contains a self-decoder followed by a cross-decoder, while retaining the overall behavior of a decoder-only Transformer.

The self-decoder creates a global key-value cache that the cross-decoder reuses through cross-attention. Caching only once substantially reduces memory demand while preserving global attention. The computation also allows prompt prefilling to exit early without changing the final output, accelerating the stage that processes the supplied context before generation.

Experiments show favorable performance relative to Transformers as model size and training-token counts increase. The authors extend YOCO to a context length of one million with near-perfect needle retrieval accuracy. Profiling reports orders-of-magnitude improvements in inference memory, prefill latency, and throughput across the studied settings. These findings link cache reuse to both long-context capability and substantial inference-efficiency gains.
neurips-2024-you-only-cache-once-decoder.tldr: YOCO shares one global key-value cache between two decoder components, reducing inference costs while supporting million-token context retrieval.
